newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican companies in Jalisco seen wary next year.
newsitem.headline: Mexican companies in Jalisco seen wary next year.

text.p: Less than 13 percent of the industrial companies in the Mexican state of Jalisco intend to make new investments next year because an uncertain economic outlook, an industry spokesman said on Monday.
"What most worries us is that less than 13 percent will invest in 1997," said Ernesto Aguirre, adviser to the National Metal Industry Chamber.
Aguirre said industrialists still did not trust government economic policy and were wary of official targets for 1997.
"There is uncertainty, i.e., the rules of the game are not yet clear," Aguirre said, "and people will not invest until there is credibility regarding the public sector."
A survey of businesses in several sectors revealed a 40 percent in sales for the year to date compared with the corresponding period of 1995, he added.
Jalisco is home to Mexico's second-largest city, Guadalajara. It is the third most industrialized state in the country.
